key_insight: A family-aware All of Us benchmark enables fairer comparisons of polygenic risk scores and genomic machine-learning models, rather than testing AI cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: Strong prediction for several diseases, including prostate cancer, supports further risk-stratification research but does not establish clinical utility.
method: Assign entire family components to fixed discovery, calibration, and test partitions.
Reserve first-degree relatives for within-family evaluation.
Separate AoU-only training from external-GWAS-assisted models and compare methods under matched data budgets.
evidence_signal: Across 14 binary disease traits in All of Us v9, the strongest scores explained 5.7–24.9% of liability-scale variance; 11 of 12 interpretable within-family effect-ratio confidence intervals included 1.
watch_item: Type 2 diabetes showed within-family attenuation (ratio 0.86, confidence interval 0.76–0.97), cautioning against assuming population-level performance fully transfers within families.
paper_title: A family-aware All of Us benchmark for polygenic prediction and genomic machine learning
